title: Load the export under payroll's names
prompt: Payroll's system uses its own column names and needs real types. The starter saves the HR export as a file; finish `solve(employees_raw)` so it reads every employee line straight into payroll's columns.
rules: Fields are separated by `;`, the first line is a header (not an employee), and quoted values can contain `;`. The fields always come in the export's order.
Payroll's columns, in order: `emp_id STRING, name STRING, title STRING, dept STRING, annual_salary DECIMAL(10,2), start_date DATE`.
Keep every employee line. A value that's missing, or can't be read as its column's type, is NULL; the rest of that line is still read.
Return only these six columns. Keep duplicate lines.
hints: A schema string gives the columns both their types and their names.
Spark matches schema columns to fields by position, so the schema's names don't have to match the header's.
With a schema, `header=True` still matters: it tells Spark to skip the first line. Think about which `mode` keeps every line.
starter:
def solve(employees_raw):
    path = "/tmp/hr/export"
    employees_raw.write.mode("overwrite").text(path)
    # Read the file at `path` into payroll's columns and return them.
    return employees_raw
explanation: One read does it all: `spark.read.csv(path, sep=";", header=True, schema="emp_id STRING, name STRING, title STRING, dept STRING, annual_salary DECIMAL(10,2), start_date DATE")`. A schema's names replace the header's, because columns are matched by position; `header=True` is still needed so the header line isn't read as an employee. The default `PERMISSIVE` mode keeps every line and sets what it can't read to NULL, so a salary of `n/a` becomes NULL while the name and date on that line are kept. Reading with `inferSchema=True` and renaming afterwards would give `annual_salary` as a double, which isn't exact for money, and `DROPMALFORMED` would lose employees payroll needs to see.
